note: File list, sizes and stated counts of https://users.cecs.anu.edu.au/~bdm/data/ and of Zenodo record 4010122, compiled for graphcat.py; descriptions written for this index.

graphs.title: All simple graphs by order
graphs.about: Every simple graph up to isomorphism, one file per order n = 2..11.

graphs-connected.title: Connected simple graphs by order
graphs-connected.about: Every connected simple graph up to isomorphism, n = 2..10.

graphs-by-edges.title: Simple graphs by number of edges
graphs-by-edges.about: Graphs with m = 1..17 edges and no isolated vertices (possibly disconnected); the label gives m.

connected-by-edges.title: Connected graphs by number of edges
connected-by-edges.about: Connected graphs with m = 1..18 edges; the label gives m.

graph-counts.title: Counts of graphs by vertices and edges
graph-counts.about: A table of the numbers of graphs by order and number of edges, up to 30 vertices.

eulerian.title: Eulerian graphs (all degrees even)
eulerian.about: Graphs with every degree even, not necessarily connected, n = 2..12.

eulerian-connected.title: Connected Eulerian graphs
eulerian-connected.about: Connected graphs with every degree even, n = 3..11.

srg.title: Strongly regular graphs
srg.about: Strongly regular graphs for some parameter sets from (25,8,3,2) to (65,32,15,16); two files may be incomplete. Smaller ones (for example (16,6,2,2)) are not here: try the vertex-transitive census.
srg.credit: made by Brendan McKay, Ted Spence or others, as the page says; Ted Spence's strongly regular graphs page has more

hypohamiltonian.title: Hypohamiltonian graphs
hypohamiltonian.about: All hypohamiltonian graphs below 18 vertices and samples on 18, 22 and 26 vertices.

cubic-hypohamiltonian.title: Cubic hypohamiltonian graphs
cubic-hypohamiltonian.about: All cubic hypohamiltonian graphs up to 26 vertices; girth at least 5 on 28 and at least 6 on 30.

planar-connected.title: Connected planar graphs
planar-connected.about: Connected planar graphs up to isomorphism (not embeddings), n = 1..11.

self-complementary.title: Self-complementary graphs
self-complementary.about: Graphs isomorphic to their complements, n = 4..17, and part of n = 20.

highly-irregular.title: Highly irregular graphs
highly-irregular.about: Connected graphs in which the neighbours of every vertex have distinct degrees, n = 1..15.

edge-critical.title: Edge-critical graphs by chromatic number
edge-critical.about: Graphs of chromatic number k that drop to k-1 when any edge is removed, n = 4..14; the label gives k.

circulant.title: Circulant graphs
circulant.about: Circulant graphs on n = 5..100 vertices as connection sets, one tar file per n with a member circN.D.txt per degree D; degrees are complete up to complement only in part of the range.

cycle-counts.title: Graphs with given numbers of cycles
cycle-counts.about: One 2-connected example for each achievable cycle count up to 100, and a cubic planar version.

min-bipartization.title: Triangle-free graphs hardest to make bipartite
min-bipartization.about: Triangle-free graphs that need the most edge deletions to become bipartite, up to 23 vertices.

ramsey.title: Ramsey graphs
ramsey.about: Graphs with no clique of size s and no independent set of size t: all Ramsey(3,4), (3,5), (3,6), (4,4) graphs by order; the largest Ramsey(3,7), (3,8), (3,9), (4,5); known Ramsey(4,6) and (5,5) graphs.

ramsey-hypergraphs.title: Ramsey(4,4;3) hypergraphs
ramsey-hypergraphs.about: 3-uniform hypergraphs with 1 to 3 edges on every 4 vertices, n = 4..12 (some files limited by edge count).

regular-induced.title: Graphs without large regular induced subgraphs
regular-induced.about: Largest known graphs with no regular induced subgraph on at least k (ge) or exactly k (eq) vertices.
regular-induced.credit: joint work of Brendan McKay and Paul Dyson

ramsey-tournaments.title: Ramsey tournaments
ramsey-tournaments.about: Largest tournaments with no transitive subtournament of order k, k = 3..7.

digraphs.title: All digraphs by order
digraphs.about: Every digraph up to isomorphism, n = 1..6, without loops and with loops allowed.

oriented.title: Oriented graphs by order
oriented.about: Digraphs without 2-cycles, n = 1..7 without loops and n = 1..6 with loops allowed.

tournaments.title: All tournaments by order
tournaments.about: Every tournament up to isomorphism, n = 2..10.

self-converse-tournaments.title: Self-converse tournaments
self-converse-tournaments.about: Tournaments isomorphic to their converse, n = 2..13.

regular-tournaments.title: Regular and semi-regular tournaments
regular-tournaments.about: Regular (odd n) and semi-regular (even n) tournaments, n = 3..13.

doubly-regular-tournaments.title: Doubly regular tournaments
doubly-regular-tournaments.about: Doubly regular tournaments, complete up to 27 vertices and partial lists for 31..51.
doubly-regular-tournaments.credit: first found up to 27 vertices by Ted Spence (recomputed by McKay); the larger lists come from skew Hadamard matrices in Christos Koukouvinos's catalogue

locally-transitive-tournaments.title: Locally transitive tournaments
locally-transitive-tournaments.about: Tournaments whose in- and out-neighbourhoods are all transitive, n = 3..20.

acyclic-digraphs.title: Acyclic digraphs
acyclic-digraphs.about: Acyclic digraphs with vertices in topological order, n = 2..8.

eulerian-digraphs.title: Connected Eulerian digraphs
eulerian-digraphs.about: Connected loopless digraphs with in-degree equal to out-degree, n = 2..8, and the oriented ones, n = 3..9.

posets.title: Posets (Hasse diagrams)
posets.format: text: n, number of covers, cover pairs
posets.about: Partially ordered sets on 1..10 points as Hasse diagrams; the line '4 2 02 13' means 0<2 and 1<3.

vertex-transitive-tournaments.title: Vertex-transitive tournaments
vertex-transitive-tournaments.about: Circulant tournaments on 1..49 vertices, and the vertex-transitive ones that are not circulant.

nonreconstructible-digraphs.title: Nonreconstructible digraphs
nonreconstructible-digraphs.about: Known digraphs not determined by their deck (or reduced deck), 3..8 vertices; consecutive lines form the pairs or triples with equal decks.

trees.title: Trees by order and diameter
trees.about: Every tree on n = 4..22 vertices with diameter D, as edge lists; one tar per order holds all diameters.

homeomorphically-irreducible-trees.title: Homeomorphically irreducible trees
homeomorphically-irreducible-trees.about: Trees with no vertex of degree 2 (series-reduced trees), n = 4..30.

latin-squares.title: Latin squares, rectangles, loops, Graeco-Latin squares
latin-squares.about: Reduced Latin squares, isotopy and main class representatives, classes with nontrivial symmetry, squares without intercalates, loops, Graeco-Latin squares and Latin rectangles, mostly orders 2..9.

latin-hypercubes.title: Latin hypercubes
latin-hypercubes.about: One representative of each main class of Latin hypercubes of small order n and dimension d (the file name repeats n d times).
latin-hypercubes.credit: computed by Brendan McKay and Ian Wanless

hadamard.title: Hadamard matrices
hadamard.format: text: one hexadecimal number per row
hadamard.about: Equivalence classes of Hadamard matrices of orders 4..32 (rows in hexadecimal; 0 bits are -1).
hadamard.credit: the matrices of order 32 were determined by Hadi Kharaghani and Behruz Tayfeh-Rezaie

nonhamiltonian-planar-cubic.title: Nonhamiltonian planar cubic graphs
nonhamiltonian-planar-cubic.about: Smallest 3-connected nonhamiltonian planar cubic graphs with extra conditions (no triangles; cyclically 4- or 5-connected); the file name encodes the class.

hypohamiltonian-planar.title: Planar hypohamiltonian and a-edge cubic graphs
hypohamiltonian-planar.about: Cubic planar hypohamiltonian graphs on 70 vertices (girth 4), and cubic planar graphs with an edge on every hamiltonian cycle, 16..38 vertices.
hypohamiltonian-planar.credit: the first 70-vertex graph was found by Araya and Wiener, six more by Mohammadreza Jooyandeh and McKay

extremal.title: Extremal graphs without given cycle lengths
extremal.about: Graphs with the largest number of edges (the Turan number) on n vertices with no cycle of the lengths in H; the label gives H, the file name n and the edge count. '.some': the edge count is exact but graphs may be missing; '.maybe': not proved extremal.
extremal.credit: joint work of Narjess Afzaly and Brendan McKay

dissociated.title: Largest dissociated sets of 0-1 vectors
dissociated.about: Largest dissociated sets of n-vectors, n = 2..7, as bipartite graphs: n column vertices, then one vertex per vector, joined to its 1 positions.

vertex-transitive.title: Vertex-transitive graphs on 10 to 47 vertices
vertex-transitive.format: tar of gzipped graph6, one file per degree
vertex-transitive.about: Every vertex-transitive graph on n = 10..47 vertices (connected or not), from the census of Royle and Holt; one tar per n on Zenodo with one gzipped graph6 file per degree k. The data does not mark Cayley graphs.
vertex-transitive.credit: Gordon Royle and Derek Holt (Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.4010122)
